answer: An agent economy can tie each identity to one licensed charcoal kiln on a named summit slope, where the holder tends a slow earth burn that cannot be rushed. A beacon sensor logs the ember temperature through the whole firing, and an inspector visits unannounced to check the burn in person. One burner cannot tend two kilns at once, and the license fee in outside money doubles per kiln on the same funding trail, so each extra fake identity costs another real kiln, another burner's week, and twice the prior fee.
